# Onboard a new customer

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

After an approved customer agreement or subscription is ready for implementation. A verified first-value outcome and an accepted handover to ongoing support and account ownership.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Reconcile the sales-to-delivery handoff

agent-runnable


Collect the signed scope, customer sponsor, intended users, promised outcomes, billing terms and implementation constraints. Resolve unsupported promises before treating the handoff as an approved delivery plan.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree the implementation plan

human · human approval required


The customer and delivery owner confirm milestones, responsibilities, data access, training and acceptance criteria. Route additional scope or sensitive integrations through their approval processes.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Configure approved access and implementation settings

manual form/portal · human approval required · hard to undo


Authorized operators provision the contracted features and least-privilege roles. Test imports or integrations in an appropriate environment and retain evidence of any required customer authorization.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Guide users to the first agreed outcome

human · human approval required


Deliver the agreed training and supervised workflow with the customer. Record actual task completion and user feedback rather than marking onboarding complete because an invitation was sent.

- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Verify acceptance and transfer ongoing ownership

agent-runnable


Confirm the agreed outcome, unresolved actions, support contacts and billing readiness. Record the customer acceptance or exception and assign the owner of adoption, renewal and future requests.

- Verify: A verified first-value outcome and an accepted handover to ongoing support and account ownership.
- Sources: [GitLab customer onboarding](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/segment/cse/customer-onboarding/) · [GitLab customer success management handbook](https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/customer-experience/csm/)
